source.title: Towards mechanistic understanding in a data-driven weather model: internal activations reveal interpretable physical features

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares single-neuron probes with SAE-feature probes in GraphCast. The results qualify the idea that neurons alone are useful units of analysis: a neuron probe performs very poorly for tropical-cyclone detection, while neuron activations are more informative for atmospheric rivers. It does not audit neuron-pole job counts.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses polysemantic neurons and compares single-neuron and SAE-feature probes. It does not measure the fraction of neurons with one or more jobs, test Qwen3, assess other language models, investigate the InceptionV1 examples, or build attribution graphs. The reported weather-feature steering and conservation results do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: Not a test. The study trains SAEs on GraphCast, a 36.7M-parameter weather GNN rather than a language model, and mentions polysemantic neurons only as motivation. It never audits the share of neurons with one main job, so V1/V2 (language-model pole shares) are not tested. It does not touch the InceptionV1 examples (V3), interpretability shares across architectures or tools (V4), neuron attribution graphs (V5), or explanation scoring (V6/V7). Its single-neuron vs SAE-feature probe comparison for tropical cyclones and atmospheric rivers is a related but different construct: the best single unit per phenomenon, not the prevalence of interpretable neurons.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SAEs extract highly interpretable physical features from GraphCast, including tropical cyclones, atmospheric rivers, sea ice and diurnal/seasonal patterns. They also conclude that amplifying or attenuating a tropical-cyclone feature changes storm predictions monotonically while largely preserving mass conservation and force balance, except at the largest amplification. They say a general claim about spontaneous interpretability is not justified by their single-model analysis.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies k-sparse autoencoders and sparse probes to internal GraphCast activations; it does not reproduce the Qwen3 neuron-pole audit or test language-model neuron explanations.
record.method_sensitivity: For tropical-cyclone probes, the paper reports that an intermediate SAE latent size (nl=2048 or 4096) seems optimal and hypothesizes that larger dictionaries may split features. Atmospheric-river SAE results show no clear trend across hyperparameter choices.

fits_no_version.finding: In GraphCast layer 8, the best single neuron detects tropical cyclones at F1 0.01, while the best SAE feature (k=32, nl=4096) reaches 0.48. For atmospheric rivers, a neuron probe reaches a competitive F1 0.30.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a weather GNN, whether a single neuron cleanly encodes a physical phenomenon depends on the phenomenon; SAE features greatly outperform neurons for tropical cyclones but not clearly for atmospheric rivers.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features in GraphCast include grid-locked features tied to the icosahedral mesh refinement rather than to weather content.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture (multi-scale mesh) induces uninterpretable, architecture-tied directions in a weather GNN's activations.

record.problems: The analysis is limited to one weather model and selected phenomena; it does not systematically estimate the prevalence of neuron-level interpretability. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the cited probe scores, and several other results are presented primarily in figures.

untested.parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit shares (about 90% / 7% / 2–4%); no neuron job-share audit in any model.
No language models, dense or MoE, and no scale comparison.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron reanalysis.
No interpretable-neuron shares across architectures, regularization or tools.
No attribution graphs from neurons and no comparison against a replacement model.
No test of explanations from activating examples against held-out firing.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 link and limits_scope label are wrong. A best-neuron probe score for one phenomenon in a weather model cannot speak to neuron job shares in Qwen3-32B or other language models. All verdict labels are removed. Atmospheric blocking found no good SAE feature (best F1 0.1); this is irrelevant to the versions. No uncertainty is reported for any F1 score.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B audit and its reported shares of one-job, two-job, and not-understood poles are not tested. The relevant result is limited to single-neuron probing for weather phenomena in GraphCast.
The study analyzes a weather model, not other language models; it does not compare dense and mixture-of-experts language models or scale.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car examples or pose interpretation are studied.
The paper reports grid-locked SAE features, but does not test neuron interpretability shares across architectures, regularization, tools, or model sizes, nor the InceptionV1 estimates.
The study intervenes on an SAE feature, not attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons; it does not compare with a trained replacement model or reconstruction error.
It does not test whether explanations fitted to activating examples predict other activations.
It does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: GraphCast
rows.operation_detail: A single SAE feature was used by a logistic probe to predict tropical-cyclone presence.
rows.note: The paper reports this as the best single feature for the stated SAE configuration.
rows.check: SAE-feature probe F1 (0.48) measures the study's own SAE method, not neuron job shares. It is a selected best value, not a V1 measure. Relink from V1 to none.

rows.subject: GraphCast
rows.operation_detail: A logistic probe trained only on single neuron activations predicted tropical-cyclone presence.
rows.note: Compared with the SAE-feature probe, the single-neuron probe was reported to perform far worse.
rows.check: The best single-neuron TC probe F1 is 0.01. This is the best neuron for one phenomenon and says nothing about what share of GraphCast neurons have one main job. It is also not a language model. Relink from V1 to none; 'absent' is not meaningful against V1.

rows.subject: GraphCast
rows.operation_detail: A probe trained on neuron activations predicted atmospheric-river presence.
rows.note: The paper calls this competitive: it is worse than all but one SAE configuration, unlike the very weak neuron-only result for tropical cyclones.
rows.check: The neuron-activation AR probe has F1 0.30, which the paper calls competitive. As with R2, it bears on no version. Relink from V1 to none.

rows.subject: GraphCast
rows.operation_detail: The second-best SAE feature for atmospheric-river detection was examined.
rows.value: The paper says its F1 scores are lower than those of the best tropical-cyclone features; no numeric F1 value is stated in the text.
rows.note: The feature is described as activating with integrated vapor transport; it was chosen for visualization instead of the highest-F1 feature because the latter activated more sparsely.
rows.check: This is a feature selected for visualization (second-best, feature 1820), with no numeric value. It should not be a result row, or should be marked as selection.

rows.subject: GraphCast
rows.operation_detail: The study identified SAE features activating on the graph grid structure.
rows.value: The authors report that grid-locked features are present and describe them as activating on the grid structure.
rows.note: The paper calls these features undesirable from an interpretability perspective; it leaves their modeling implications open.
rows.check: The presence of grid-locked SAE features is described only qualitatively. It bears on no version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GraphCast single-neuron probing for tropical-cyclone presence
reader_labels.reason: The single-neuron probe is essentially randomized (R2), unlike the SAE-feature probe (R1), so the study qualifies how useful neurons are as units of analysis for this task; it does not estimate the share of neurons with a main job.
